title: A coordinated dining furniture project
intro: A dining set needs functional and visual coordination across table, chairs and sideboard. Turn those decisions into a traceable drawing, procurement, sample and inspection package.
goals: Connect the pieces through a use scenario
Translate design intent into acceptance criteria

sections.title: Connect the pieces through a use scenario
sections.text: Define everyday meals, guests, serving and clearing away. Assign each piece a role and list the sideboard contents and requirement owner. Check chair arms against the table underside and sideboard doors against pulled-out chairs. A matching finish cannot compensate for an incompatible functional interface.
sections.caption: Review the pieces together in the same use scenario.

sections.title: Link drawings to procurement records
sections.text: Assign type codes T for table, C for chair and S for sideboard. Record quantity, approved dimensions, material, finish, drawing/revision reference and missing product information. One table, four chairs and one sideboard means ⁦1 + 4 + 1 = 6⁩ physical pieces but three types. Do not confuse quantities with type or drawing counts; distinguish any different chair product.
sections.caption: Three types, six physical pieces in the exercise.

sections.title: Translate design intent into acceptance criteria
sections.text: Code the finish sample and review it alongside chair materials under relevant project lighting. Acceptance criteria should reference approved dimensions and samples, hardware movement, edge quality and seating/serving interfaces. Each piece needs appropriate performance documentation and review. Record defects, owners, corrective actions and reinspection evidence before closing an item.
sections.caption: Close defects with referenced correction and reinspection evidence.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: Chair C changes to an armchair while its quantity remains four. Its arm no longer clears the underside of table T. The six-piece quantity is still correct, but the functional package is not. Update the chair reference, review the T/C interface and obtain renewed selection approval.
example.decision: Decision: a product change reopens its interfaces even when quantity is unchanged.

quiz.question: One table, four chairs and one sideboard: how many types and pieces?
quiz.explanation: The chair is one type repeated four times.

assignment.prompt: Submit a use layout, type/quantity/revision schedule, sample card and one defect/correction record.

faq.question: Does matching colour establish a coordinated set?
faq.answer: No. Functional interfaces, materials, details and procurement references must also align.
